#### 1. Usher syndrome  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.782)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-9662360, Reactome:R-HSA-9662361, Reactome:R-HSA-2453902)

**Proposed mechanism:** Pathogenic MYO7A variant (HGVS:NM_000260.3:c.1234G>A) —DISRUPTS→ MYO7A (HGNC:7606); MYO7A (HGNC:7606) —DISRUPTS→ Stereocilia maintenance and function (GO:0001770); Stereocilia maintenance and function (GO:0001770) —LEADS_TO→ Hair cell dysfunction (HP:0000365); Hair cell dysfunction (HP:0000365) —LEADS_TO→ Hearing impairment (HP:0000388); Stereocilia maintenance and function (GO:0001770) —LEADS_TO→ Retinal degeneration (HP:0000479). Pathogenic variants in MYO7A disrupt the stereocilia maintenance and function in inner ear hair cells, leading to hearing impairment. In Usher syndrome, MYO7A dysfunction also affects retinal photoreceptor function, causing progressive vision loss.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in MYO7A that lead to a gain-of-function or dominant-negative effect, rather than loss-of-function, would falsify this hypothesis. Additionally, if the identified MYO7A variants are exclusively associated with either hearing loss or vision loss without overlap, despite being pathogenic, it would challenge the proposed shared mechanism. _(variant: High frequency (>= 0.01) of a specific pathogenic variant in gnomAD affecting MYO7A, suggesting it is not solely disease-causing.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared MYO7A mechanism provides a potential therapeutic target for both nonsyndromic hearing loss 11 and Usher syndrome. Gene therapy or small molecule approaches aimed at restoring MYO7A function or compensating for its loss could offer benefit to patients with either condition.
